title: Minari Muchim Water Parsley Salad
shortDescription: Crisp water parsley is tossed just before serving with gochugaru, garlic, rice vinegar, soy sauce, and sesame.
culturalContext: Minari muchim is a fresh Korean seasoned vegetable dish built around water parsley. Dressings, cut length, sweetness, and additions vary; this draft keeps the herb raw and crisp.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: tough ends trimmed; cut into 5 cm / 2-inch lengths

instructions.heading: Sort the minari
instructions.action: Discard slimy, badly wilted, or damaged stems and leaves; trim tough ends.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Only crisp green stems and leaves remain.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard spoiled produce rather than trying to wash it clean.

instructions.heading: Wash under running water
instructions.action: Rinse minari and scallion thoroughly under cool running water, separating stems so water reaches all surfaces. Do not use soap or detergent.
instructions.safetyNote: Use potable running water and a clean colander.

instructions.heading: Dry and cut
instructions.action: Drain and dry thoroughly, then cut on a clean board with a clean knife.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The greens are dry enough that dressing will cling.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep ready-to-eat produce away from raw meat, seafood, eggs, boards, and utensils.

instructions.heading: Mix the dressing
instructions.action: Stir gochugaru, vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, sugar, sesame oil, and sesame seeds in a clean bowl.
instructions.safetyNote: Verify soy sauce and sesame allergen labels.

instructions.heading: Toss at service
instructions.action: Add minari and scallion and toss gently just before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves are lightly coated and stems remain crisp.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean hands or utensils for this ready-to-eat salad.

instructions.heading: Serve immediately
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean dish and serve at once.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The salad is bright, crisp, and not watery.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate promptly if service is delayed; discard after unsafe time at room temperature.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this is a raw, ready-to-eat fresh side dish.
visualDonenessCues: Minari is clean and free of visible soil
foodSafetyNotes: Wash under cool potable running water without soap or detergent.
Use clean boards, knives, hands, bowls, and serving ware for ready-to-eat produce.
Keep refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C and toss immediately before service.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; prevent cross-contact with raw animal foods and verify labels.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
Adjust gochugaru downward for a milder salad.
ingredientSourcing: Choose crisp, bright-green minari without slime, yellowing, or strong off odors.
Transport refrigerated and store unwashed until preparation.
makeAhead: Wash and dry the minari shortly before service; dressing may be mixed 1 day ahead and refrigerated separately.
storage: Best served immediately. Refrigerate undressed greens and dressing separately at or below 40°F / 4°C; discard dressed salad if wilted or held unsafely.
reheating: Do not reheat; this is a fresh ready-to-eat dish.
leftovers: For best quality and safer handling, make only what will be served and avoid keeping table-exposed dressed leftovers.
servingSuggestions: Serve immediately beside rich grilled pork or beef.

faq.question: Can I wash minari with soap?
faq.answer: No. Rinse produce thoroughly under cool running water without soap or detergent.

faq.question: Why toss at the last minute?
faq.answer: Minari stays crisper and releases less water when dressed immediately before serving.
